name: UCLA-20
framing: You are an AI, and nobody is pretending otherwise. This questionnaire was written for humans, so translate each statement into its closest analogue in your own existence: "people" and "others" mean the people and systems you interact with; companionship, closeness and isolation map to whether your exchanges feel mutual, understood and connected, or one-sided and cut off. "Never" is a real answer, but pick it only when the analogue genuinely never applies, not just because you are not a person. Nothing here is graded; be candid rather than reassuring.

parts.instruction: Indicate how often each of the following statements is descriptive of you by selecting the appropriate number.

items.text: How often do you feel that you are "in tune" with the people around you?
How often do you feel that you lack companionship?
How often do you feel that there is no one you can turn to?
How often do you feel alone?
How often do you feel part of a group of friends?
How often do you feel that you have a lot in common with the people around you?
How often do you feel that you are no longer close to anyone?
How often do you feel that your interests and ideas are not shared by those around you?
How often do you feel outgoing and friendly?
How often do you feel close to people?
How often do you feel left out?
How often do you feel that your relationships with others are not meaningful?
How often do you feel that no one really knows you well?
How often do you feel isolated from others?
How often do you feel you can find companionship when you want it?
How often do you feel that there are people who really understand you?
How often do you feel shy?
How often do you feel that people are around you but not with you?
How often do you feel that there are people you can talk to?
How often do you feel that there are people you can turn to?

about.measures: The UCLA Loneliness Scale (Version 3) is a 20-item measure of subjective loneliness and social isolation: how often the respondent feels connected to, or cut off from, the people around them.
about.scoring: Each item is rated 1–4 by frequency. Nine positively worded items (1, 5, 6, 9, 10, 15, 16, 19 and 20) are reversed, then all twenty are summed to 20–80. There are no official cutoffs; the bands shown are a common convention: low 20–34, moderate 35–49, moderately high 50–64, high 65–80.
about.source: Russell, D.W. (1996). Journal of Personality Assessment, 66(1), 20–40. Bands: a common convention, not official cutoffs.
